title: LIVE WTA Finals 2026 | Mirra Andreeva takes on Diana Shnaider after last-minute change
text:
Mirra Andreeva makes light work of last-minute WTA Finals replacement to complete perfect run Skip to content Tournaments ▼ Newsletter FAQ Calendars ▼ Players ▼ Originals ▼ Live Scores Mirra Andreeva makes light work of last-minute WTA Finals replacement to complete perfect run
 WTA by Cristhián Avila Friday, 13 November 2026 at 22:16 Follow us on Google! 0 Mirra Andreeva completed a perfect group-stage campaign at the 2026 WTA Finals , defeating Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-2 to secure her third consecutive victory in Indian Wells. The World No. 3 had initially been scheduled to face Karolina Muchova , but the Czech's withdrawal due to gastrointestinal illness shortly before the match resulted in an unexpected change of opponent. ARTICLE_IN_2
 --> 
 Shnaider, the tournament's second alternate, was called upon at the last minute and had little time to prepare for an appearance she had not anticipated. The Russian had not even expected to compete, making the circumstances particularly challenging against an opponent who had already secured her place in the semifinals with impressive victories over Elina Svitolina and Aryna Sabalenka. Nevertheless, Shnaider made a promising start, breaking Andreeva in the opening game before consolidating for a 2-0 advantage. However, her early momentum quickly faded as the teenager found her rhythm and began to dictate proceedings from the baseline. Andreeva responded with greater consistency and precision, exposing her compatriot's lack of match preparation. 
 The World No. 3 eventually won the opening set 6-2 and maintained her dominance after the change of ends. Shnaider struggled to find answers as Andreeva continued to apply pressure on her serve, completing a comfortable straight-sets victory. 6 games in a row 👊
Mirra Andreeva is on a mission as she takes the opening set against Shnaider 6-2!

 Andreeva sets up semifinal meeting with Pegula
 The turning point came early in the opening set, when Shnaider was unable to consolidate her initial break. A double fault while facing a break point handed Andreeva the opportunity to get back on serve, and the teenager immediately took advantage to move ahead. From there, she increasingly controlled the rallies, forcing Shnaider into difficult positions and capitalizing on her opponent's errors. Andreeva's shot selection also stood out, particularly when she moved forward to finish points at the net. A superb drop shot helped her secure another break in the first set, while a forehand winner down the line allowed her to close out the opener after Shnaider failed to execute her own attempt at a drop shot. ARTICLE_IN_2

 The second set offered little change in the overall pattern. Shnaider managed to hold her opening service game, but Andreeva quickly regained control, breaking twice more and leaving her compatriot with few opportunities to recover. Another double fault from Shnaider ultimately handed Andreeva the final break and sealed the 6-2, 6-2 result. With the victory, Andreeva became the only player at this year's WTA Finals to win all three round-robin matches.
